newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: Long awaited U.S. economic data sent conflicting signals to bond markets, leaving French bonds slightly lower on Friday with traders cautious ahead of monetary policy meetings in both German and United States next week.
Traders said confusion about the data in terms of implications for U.S. interest rates led investors to avoid taking straight directional punts, preferring rather to look at spread trades.
Some futures traders said while the overall mood in the futures pits was somewhat bearish there was a certain reluctance to short the French market for fear of a U.S. bond rise.

"The feeling is we've gone a long way. We're getting such conflicting data and ricocheting all over the place that people are doing curve trades and limiting the directional plays," Joanne Perez, strategist at Merrill Lynch in Paris said.
French bond futures shrugged off a stronger-than-expected rise in fourth quarter U.S. gross domestic product. Analysts said the tame price deflator mitigated the impact of the strong growth.
The reverse was the case for a U.S. Chicago purchasing managers index which was weaker than feared but with a sharp rise in the price paid component.

"The economy was strong but inflation was low. It hasn't advanced the debate that much," Andrew Milligan at General Accident said. "I can't see (the Federal Reserve) moving in February, maybe in March."

French bond futures dipped lower on the GDP release before climbing into the purchasing managers release. They spiked higher on the second report before drifting back slightly to settle down 0.06 at 130.48.
One trader said he expected the contract to start strongly next week and move back towards 131.00 although others were more bearish.
The short end of the curve was the worst hit on Friday following Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet's statement that interest rates were on hold for now.

PIBOR traders said there was widespread selling, especially by some non-resident funds, which sent the March contract as low as 96.66, down nine basis points. The spread over Euromarks widened to 21 basis points from 13 on Thursday.

Some analysts said they still expected the Bank of France to move in the coming weeks, narrowing the gap between French and German rates, making June PIBOR a relatively good buy after a 10 basis point slump on Friday.

"The short end has obviously taken a big hit after Trichet," Perez said. "But I suspect he's being a bit stubborn. I still think this 10 basis point gap (over German repo rate) will be seen by the majority of members of the (policy) council as being superfluous."
She said she expected another cut in the intervention rate by the end of February. The franc remained little changed against the mark at 3.3753 compared with 3.3747.
Call money was lowered to 3-1/8 1/4 percent in a move seen as technical after the intervention rate cut on Thursday.
